title: NeuraChip: Accelerating GNN Computations with a Hash-based Decoupled Spatial Accelerator
problem: Graph Neural Networks exhibit irregular sparsity patterns that cause unbalanced compute resource utilization in sparse matrix multiplication operations. Prior accelerators using look-ahead buffers for prefetching suffer from inefficient on-chip memory utilization and redundant data residency.
motivation: GNNs are critical for processing non-euclidean data in domains like social networks and bioinformatics, but their adoption is limited by scalability challenges on large-scale graphs.
method: NeuraChip uses Gustavson's algorithm to decouple multiplication and addition computations in sparse matrix multiplication, enabling independent exploitation of their data dependencies. A rolling eviction strategy mitigates memory bloat by reducing data idling in on-chip memory. Dynamic reseeding hash-based mapping achieves load balancing uniform across compute resources regardless of sparsity patterns.
key_novelty: Decoupling sparse matrix multiplication into independent multiplication and addition stages with rolling eviction and hash-based load balancing for sparsity-agnostic resource utilization.
contributions: Spatial accelerator architecture decoupling multiplication and addition for GNN acceleration
Rolling eviction strategy for reducing memory bloat in sparse computations
Hash-based dynamic load balancing for uniform resource utilization
NeuraSim open-source cycle-accurate simulator for performance analysis

metrics.speedup: 22.1× vs Intel MKL, 17.1× vs cuSPARSE, 16.7× vs hipSPARSE, 1.5× vs prior SpGEMM accelerators, 1.3× vs prior GNN accelerators

primary_theme: Decoupled spatial accelerator for sparse GNN computations
